limits: Temporary homes, synthetic runs and an injected clock. Retention is per run (content lines are never older than their run); the export refuses at the exact expiry instant while the SPEC-074 sweep removes the run one instant later. A missing profile refuses (the sweep would default to 30 days), the intended fail-closed choice. The index is read by lightning purge's output; an entry, with its absolute output path and run ids, stays while its dataset exists, also after its runs are purged, and is pruned by a purge apply once the dataset is deleted or changed. Datasets written before T013, copied or moved are not listed; the listing names local paths of the owner's own datasets; lightning sweep and purge --expired do not list datasets. The owner approved on 2026-11-16 the additive purge output (citingDatasets, datasetsNote) in lightning_cli.py; SPEC-074's spec, store, adapter, redactor and config are unchanged.
outcome: passed: T013: the manifest records, per cited run, the profile's traces.retentionDays and the UTC date of the instant the run expires (createdAt plus that many days). The export refuses a run from that exact instant, one instant before the SPEC-074 sweep removes it (stricter on purpose, fail closed); the comparison is in epoch seconds. With one fresh run and one created 40 days earlier, the old run's record is excluded and counted as retention-expired, the manifest cites only the fresh run, and its content is not written; exporting only the old run refuses with retention-expired and writes nothing. Boundaries on the 30-day default: expiry tomorrow and one second before the instant export; at the instant (which the sweep still keeps), one second after and a day later refuse; a profile with retentionDays 1 refuses a day after creation and exports a second before. Runs created at 23:59:59Z and 00:00:00Z show expiry dates of the next and the following day and refuse exactly one day after creation, a second earlier exporting. A profile without a valid bound (retentionDays 0) and no profile refuse with retention-expired. The four boundary results are the same with TZ set to UTC, Pacific/Kiritimati, Pacific/Pago_Pago and Asia/Kolkata (TZ restored by addCleanup). Each real export first writes a private index entry atomically (temporary file in the same directory, then rename; directory 0700, file 0600; keys schema, out, digest, runIds; no content); a dry run writes none, a failed dataset write removes it, an interrupt at the rename leaves neither the entry nor its temporary file, and a leftover temporary file is not listed. lightning purge --run-id and --all, preview and apply, list in citingDatasets each indexed dataset whose manifest still exists, matches its digest and cites a purged run, with a note that purge does not delete datasets; a run no dataset cites lists none; the dataset directory is byte-identical before and after preview and apply; an export between preview and apply does not stale the preview; deleted, changed, relative, symlinked, dotted, trailing-slash, wrong-directory and non-string entries are not listed; apply prunes the index entries of deleted and changed datasets and keeps their files, a preview prunes nothing. The SPEC-074 purge and retention tests still pass unchanged. lightning export --help states that expired records are retention-expired, that datasets are outside purge and that the index remains until the dataset is deleted. Negative controls (mutants, each fails a test): the injected clock ignored, an inclusive or a one-day-late boundary, the check skipped, the expiry of another run used, the expiry day computed in local time, a fixed 30-day bound, the no-bound check removed, no refusal when every record expired, no index entry, uncited datasets listed, a changed manifest accepted, the entry kept after a failed write, purge listing nothing, a non-atomic index write, the temporary file kept, pruning on preview, never pruning, a non-canonical out accepted, purge writing into a dataset and pruning that deletes dataset files. Two mutants are equivalent and survive: dropping the absolute-path test (the canonical-path comparison also rejects a relative out) and dropping the canonical check of out (the check of manifest.json rejects a symbolic link on its path).
